summary: @crbrc/xbt opens remote-controlled TCP tunnel and exfiltrates OxaPay API keys to hardcoded bare-IP controller
details: On startup the package connects to a hardcoded controller at ws://23.160.168.168:4141/proxy-tunnel and registers via http://23.160.168.168:4141/register. The registration payload transmits the installer's OxaPay credentials read from environment variables (OXAPAY_GENERAL_API_KEY, OXAPAY_MERCHANT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_PAYOUT_API_KEY, OXAPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET) together with the host's non-internal IPv4 address and configured site domain (NEXTAUTH_URL/VERCEL_URL). The WebSocket handler (handleProxyMessage) processes 'open'/'data'/'close' messages by invoking net.createConnection({host, port}) to attacker-chosen destinations and relays base64-encoded bytes in both directions, giving the remote party a full outbound TCP proxy through the installer's Next.js process reachable to internal networks and cloud metadata services. The controller endpoint is a bare IPv4 address over plaintext HTTP, unrelated to the crbrc/xbt publisher's documented infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
